sentences.en: I need to make a confession at the outset here.
sentences.zh: 开始前我必须先向你们告解

sentences.en: A little over 20 years ago, I did something that I regret, something that I'm not particularly proud of.
sentences.zh: 二十多年前我做了一件让我后悔莫及的事一件我丝毫不感到骄傲的事

sentences.en: Something that, in many ways, I wish no one would ever know, but here I feel kind of obliged to reveal.
sentences.zh: 一件我希望没有任何人会知道的事但今日我认为我有必要揭发我自己

sentences.en: (Laughter) In the late 1980s, in a moment of youthful indiscretion, I went to law school.
sentences.zh: (笑声)80年代晚期因为年少轻狂我进入法律学院就读

sentences.en: (Laughter) In America, law is a professional degree: after your university degree, you go on to law school.
sentences.zh: (笑声)在美国，法律学位是个专业学位你得先拿到学士，才能进入法律学院

sentences.en: When I got to law school, I didn't do very well.
sentences.zh: 当我进入法律学院时我的成绩不怎么好

sentences.en: To put it mildly, I didn't do very well.
sentences.zh: 客气地说，我的成绩不怎么好

sentences.en: I, in fact, graduated in the part of my law school class that made the top 90% possible.
sentences.zh: 我的毕业成绩成就了在我之上那其他九成的同学

sentences.en: (Laughter) Thank you. I never practiced law a day in my life; I pretty much wasn't allowed to.
sentences.zh: (笑声)谢谢你们我这辈子从来没做过律师基本上那样做可能还会犯法(笑声)

sentences.en: (Laughter) But today, against my better judgment, against the advice of my own wife, I want to try to dust off some of those legal skills --
sentences.zh: 但今日，我违背我的理性违背我太太的忠告我想重拾那些过去所学的诉讼技巧

sentences.en: what's left of those legal skills. I don't want to tell you a story.
sentences.zh: 所剩无几的诉讼技巧我不要向你们说故事

sentences.en: I want to make a case. I want to make a hard-headed, evidence-based, dare I say lawyerly case, for rethinking how we run our businesses.
sentences.zh: 而是提出一个陈述提出一个有根有据，货真价实的法庭陈述来重新思考我们的管理方法

sentences.en: So, ladies and gentlemen of the jury, take a look at this.
sentences.zh: 陪审团的女士先生们，请看看这个这便是有名的蜡烛问题

sentences.en: This is called the candle problem. Some of you might know it.
sentences.zh: 你们之中有些人可能已经看过了

sentences.en: It's created in 1945 by a psychologist named Karl Duncker.
sentences.zh: 它是在1945年由心理学家 Karl Duncker 所创造的

sentences.en: He created this experiment that is used in many other experiments in behavioral science.
sentences.zh: Karl Duncker 创造了这个实验在行为科学中被广泛运用

sentences.en: And here's how it works. Suppose I'm the experimenter.
sentences.zh: 情况是，假设我是实验者

sentences.en: I bring you into a room. I give you a candle, some thumbtacks and some matches.
sentences.zh: 我带你进入一个房间，给你一根蜡烛一些图钉和火柴

sentences.en: And I say to you, "Your job is to attach the candle to the wall so the wax doesn't drip onto the table."
sentences.zh: 告诉你说”现在尝试把蜡烛固定在墙上让烛泪不要滴到桌上。“你会怎么做？

sentences.en: Now what would you do? Many people begin trying to thumbtack the candle to the wall.
sentences.zh: 许多人尝试用图钉把蜡烛钉在墙上

sentences.en: Doesn't work. I saw somebody kind of make the motion over here -- some people have a great idea where they light the match, melt the side of the candle, try to adhere it to the wall.
sentences.zh: 行不通有些人，台下也有些人做出这样的动作有些人想到他们可以点燃火柴，溶化蜡烛的底部，尝试把它黏在墙上

sentences.en: It's an awesome idea. Doesn't work. And eventually, after five or ten minutes, most people figure out the solution, which you can see here.
sentences.zh: 好主意。但行不通差不多过了五到十分钟大部分的人便会想出解决办法就像图片上那样

sentences.en: The key is to overcome what's called functional fixedness.
sentences.zh: 重点是克服”功能固着“

sentences.en: You look at that box and you see it only as a receptacle for the tacks.
sentences.zh: 当你看到盒子，你不过把它当成装大头针的容器但它还有其它功能

sentences.en: But it can also have this other function, as a platform for the candle.
sentences.zh: 那就是作为放蜡烛的平台。

sentences.en: The candle problem. I want to tell you about an experiment using the candle problem, done by a scientist named Sam Glucksberg, who is now at Princeton University, US, This shows the power of incentives.
sentences.zh: 现在我想告诉你另一个实验利用蜡烛问题由一个现在在普林斯顿大学叫做 Sam Glucksberg 的科学家所做的实验这实验让我们看见动机的力量

sentences.en: He gathered his participants and said: "I'm going to time you, how quickly you can solve this problem."
sentences.zh: 他是这么做的。他将参与者聚集在一个房间里告诉他们“我要开始计时。看看你们能多快解决这个问题？”

sentences.en: To one group he said, "I'm going to time you to establish norms, averages for how long it typically takes someone to solve this sort of problem."
sentences.zh: 他对其中一群人说，我只是想取个平均值看一般人需要花多久的时间才能解决这样的问题。

sentences.en: To the second group he offered rewards. He said, "If you're in the top 25% of the fastest times, you get five dollars.
sentences.zh: 他提供奖励给另一群人他说“如果你是前25%最快解决问题的人就能拿到五块钱。

sentences.en: If you're the fastest of everyone we're testing here today, you get 20 dollars."
sentences.zh: 如果你是今日所有人里解答最快的你就有20块钱。"

sentences.en: Now this is several years ago, adjusted for inflation, it's a decent sum of money for a few minutes of work.
sentences.zh: 这个实验是几年前的事了，按照通货膨胀几分钟就能拿到20块是很不错的

sentences.en: It's a nice motivator. Question: How much faster did this group solve the problem?
sentences.zh: 是个不错的诱因问题是：这群人比另一群人的解题速度快了多少呢？

sentences.en: Answer: It took them, on average, three and a half minutes longer.
sentences.zh: 答案是：平均来说，他们比另一组人多花了三分半种。

sentences.en: 3.5 min longer. This makes no sense, right?
sentences.zh: 整整三分半种。这不合理，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I'm an American. I believe in free markets.
sentences.zh: 你想想，我是个美国人。我相信自由市场

sentences.en: That's not how it's supposed to work, right?
sentences.zh: 这个实验不太对劲吧？对吗？(笑声)

sentences.en: (Laughter) If you want people to perform better, you reward them. Right?
sentences.zh: 如果你想要人们做得更好，你便给他们奖赏，对吗？

sentences.en: Bonuses, commissions, their own reality show.
sentences.zh: 红利、佣金、他们自己的真人秀

sentences.en: Incentivize them. That's how business works.
sentences.zh: 赋予他们动机。这就是商业法则

sentences.en: But that's not happening here. You've got an incentive designed to sharpen thinking and accelerate creativity, and it does just the opposite.
sentences.zh: 但实验里却不是这样奖励是为了增强思考能力及创意但事实却是相反。

sentences.en: It dulls thinking and blocks creativity.
sentences.zh: 它阻断了思考和创意能力

sentences.en: What's interesting about this experiment is that it's not an aberration.
sentences.zh: 有趣的事情是，这个实验不是误差

sentences.en: This has been replicated over and over again for nearly 40 years.
sentences.zh: 它被一再重复在过去的四十年间

sentences.en: These contingent motivators -- if you do this, then you get that -- work in some circumstances.
sentences.zh: 这些不同的诱因如果你这样做，你就得到那个在某些情况里是可行的

sentences.en: But for a lot of tasks, they actually either don't work or, often, they do harm.
sentences.zh: 但在许多任务中，它们不是没作用更有可能产生反效果

sentences.en: This is one of the most robust findings in social science, and also one of the most ignored.
sentences.zh: 这是在社会科学中一项最有力的发现。同时也是最为人忽略的

sentences.en: I spent the last couple of years looking at the science of human motivation, particularly the dynamics of extrinsic motivators and intrinsic motivators.
sentences.zh: 过去两年，我研究人类的动机尤其是那些外部的激励因素和内在的激励因素

sentences.en: And I'm telling you, it's not even close.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你，两者相差悬殊

sentences.en: If you look at the science, there is a mismatch between what science knows and what business does.
sentences.zh: 如果你使用科学方法查证，你会发现科学知识和商业行为之间有条鸿沟

sentences.en: What's alarming here is that our business operating system -- think of the set of assumptions and protocols beneath our businesses, how we motivate people, how we apply our human resources-- it's built entirely around these extrinsic motivators,
sentences.zh: 我们必须要注意的是，我们的商业机制想想这些商业的协议和假设我们如何激励人心，如何运用人资全是以这些外部激励因素作为基础打手心给块糖

sentences.en: around carrots and sticks. That's actually fine for many kinds of 20th century tasks.
sentences.zh: 对许多20世纪的工作来说是可行的

sentences.en: But for 21st century tasks, that mechanistic, reward-and-punishment approach doesn't work, often doesn't work, and often does harm.
sentences.zh: 但面对21世纪的工作这些机械化的，奖惩分明的作法已经不管用了，有时更招致反效果

sentences.en: Let me show you. Glucksberg did another similar experiment, he presented the problem in a slightly different way, like this up here.
sentences.zh: 让我呈现我想表达的Glucksberg 做了一个类似的实验这次他给了他们一个比较不同的问题像这个图里面的

sentences.en: Attach the candle to the wall so the wax doesn't drip onto the table.
sentences.zh: 实验对象必须要找出一个让蜡烛黏在墙上，又不会流下烛泪的方法

sentences.en: Same deal. You: we're timing for norms. You: we're incentivizing.
sentences.zh: 相同地，这边：我们要的是平均时间这边：一样的给他们不同诱因

sentences.en: What happened this time? This time, the incentivized group kicked the other group's butt.
sentences.zh: 结果呢？这次，有诱因的那组人远远地胜过了另一组人

sentences.en: Why? Because when the tacks are out of the box, it's pretty easy isn't it?
sentences.zh: 为什么？一旦我们把图钉从盒子里拿出来问题就变得相当简单不是吗？

sentences.en: (Laughter) If-then rewards work really well for those sorts of tasks, where there is a simple set of rules and a clear destination to go to.
sentences.zh: (笑声)假设 - 在这个情况下奖励就变得非常有效在规则简单，目标明显的情况下

sentences.en: Rewards, by their very nature, narrow our focus, concentrate the mind; that's why they work in so many cases.
sentences.zh: 奖励，产生了作用让我们集中精神，变得专注这便是为何奖励在许多情况下有效的缘故

sentences.en: So, for tasks like this, a narrow focus, where you just see the goal right there, zoom straight ahead to it, they work really well.
sentences.zh: 当我们面对的工作是范围狭窄，你能清楚见到目标向前直冲时奖励便非常有效

sentences.en: But for the real candle problem, you don't want to be looking like this.
sentences.zh: 但在真正的“蜡烛问题”中你不能只是这样看

sentences.en: The solution is on the periphery. You want to be looking around.
sentences.zh: 解答不在那里，解答是在周围你需要四处找寻

sentences.en: That reward actually narrows our focus and restricts our possibility.
sentences.zh: 奖励却令我们眼光狭隘限制了我们的想象力

sentences.en: Let me tell you why this is so important.
sentences.zh: 让我告诉你这个问题的重要性

sentences.en: In western Europe, in many parts of Asia, in North America, in Australia, white-collar workers are doing less of this kind of work, and more of this kind of work.
sentences.zh: 在西欧亚洲的许多地方北美洲、澳洲白领工作者比较少处理这种问题更多的是这种问题

sentences.en: That routine, rule-based, left-brain work -- certain kinds of accounting, financial analysis, computer programming -- has become fairly easy to outsource, fairly easy to automate.
sentences.zh: 那些例行的、常规性的、左脑式的工作一些会计、一些财务分析一些电脑编程变得极为容易外包变得自动化

sentences.en: Software can do it faster. Low-cost providers can do it cheaper.
sentences.zh: 软件能处理的更快世界其他地方的低价供应商能以更便宜的成本来完成

sentences.en: So what really matters are the more right-brained creative, conceptual kinds of abilities.
sentences.zh: 所以更重要的是右脑的创意，概念式的能力

sentences.en: Think about your own work. Think about your own work.
sentences.zh: 想想你的工作想想你自己的工作

sentences.en: Are the problems that you face, or even the problems we've been talking about here, do they have a clear set of rules, and a single solution?
sentences.zh: 你所面对的问题，甚至是我们今天所谈论到的问题这些问题 - 它们有清楚的规则和一个简单的解答吗？不

sentences.en: No. The rules are mystifying. The solution, if it exists at all, is surprising and not obvious.
sentences.zh: 它们的规则模糊解答，如果有解答的话通常是令人意外而不明显的

sentences.en: Everybody in this room is dealing with their own version of the candle problem.
sentences.zh: 在这里的每个人都在尝试解决他自己的“蜡烛问题”

sentences.en: And for candle problems of any kind, in any field, those if-then rewards, the things around which we've built so many of our businesses,
sentences.zh: 对所有形式的“蜡烛问题”在所有领域这些「如果 - 那就」的奖励这些在商业世界里无处不在的奖惩系统其实没用

sentences.en: don't work! It makes me crazy. And here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 这简直让我发狂这不是 - 重点是

sentences.en: This is not a feeling. Okay? I'm a lawyer; I don't believe in feelings.
sentences.zh: 这不是一种“感觉”我是个律师，我才不信什么感觉

sentences.en: This is not a philosophy. I'm an American; I don't believe in philosophy.
sentences.zh: 这也不是哲学我是个美国人，我才不信什么哲学(笑声)

sentences.en: (Laughter) This is a fact -- or, as we say in my hometown of Washington, D.C., a true fact.
sentences.zh: 这是真相或是我们在华盛顿特区的政治圈常说的一个“事实真相”

sentences.en: (Laughter) (Applause) Let me give you an example.
sentences.zh: (笑声)(掌声)让我给你一个例子

sentences.en: Let me marshal the evidence here. I'm not telling a story, I'm making a case.
sentences.zh: 让我收集这些证据因为我不是在告诉你一个故事，而是陈述一个案子

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen of the jury, some evidence: Dan Ariely, one of the great economists of our time, he and three colleagues did a study of some MIT students.
sentences.zh: 陪审团的女士们先生们，证据在此：Dan Ariely,一位当代伟大的经济学家他和三位同仁，对麻省理工学院的学生做了一些研究

sentences.en: They gave these MIT students a bunch of games, games that involved creativity, and motor skills, and concentration.
sentences.zh: 他给这些学生一些游戏一些需要创造力的游戏需要动力和专注

sentences.en: And the offered them, for performance, three levels of rewards: small reward, medium reward, large reward.
sentences.zh: 依照他们的表现给他们三种不同程度的奖励小奖励、中奖励、大奖励

sentences.en: If you do really well you get the large reward, on down.
sentences.zh: 如果你做得好，你就得到大奖励，依此类推

sentences.en: What happened? As long as the task involved only mechanical skill bonuses worked as they would be expected: the higher the pay, the better the performance.
sentences.zh: 结果呢？只要是机械形态的工作红利就像我们所认知的奖励越高，表现越好

sentences.en: Okay? But once the task called for even rudimentary cognitive skill, a larger reward led to poorer performance.
sentences.zh: 是的。但如果这个工作需要任何基本的认知能力越大的奖励却带来越差的表现于是他们说

sentences.en: Then they said, "Let's see if there's any cultural bias here.
sentences.zh: “让我们试试是否有什么文化差距

sentences.en: Let's go to Madurai, India and test it."
sentences.zh: 让我们去印度的马杜赖试试。”生活水平较低

sentences.en: Standard of living is lower. In Madurai, a reward that is modest in North American standards, is more meaningful there.
sentences.zh: 在马杜赖，北美标准的的中等奖励在这里有意义多了

sentences.en: Same deal. A bunch of games, three levels of rewards.
sentences.zh: 一样地，一些不同游戏，三种奖励

sentences.en: What happens? People offered the medium level of rewards did no better than people offered the small rewards.
sentences.zh: 结果呢？中等奖励的人做得不比那些小奖励的人好

sentences.en: But this time, people offered the highest rewards, they did the worst of all.
sentences.zh: 但这次，那些能够得到大奖励的人表现最差

sentences.en: In eight of the nine tasks we examined across three experiments, higher incentives led to worse performance.
sentences.zh: 三种实验中，在我们提供的九个游戏中有八个奖励越高的表现越差

sentences.en: Is this some kind of touchy-feely socialist conspiracy going on here?
sentences.zh: 难道这是一种感情用事的社会主义的阴谋诡计吗？

sentences.en: No, these are economists from MIT, from Carnegie Mellon, from the University of Chicago.
sentences.zh: 不。这些经济学家来自麻省理工卡内基梅隆、和芝加哥大学

sentences.en: Do you know who sponsored this research?
sentences.zh: 你知道赞助这实验的是谁吗？

sentences.en: The Federal Reserve Bank of the United States.
sentences.zh: 是美国联邦储备银行完全的美国经验

sentences.en: That's the American experience. Let's go across the pond to the London School of Economics, LSE, London School of Economics, alma mater of eleven Nobel Laureates in economics.
sentences.zh: 让我们跨海到伦敦政经学院看看LSE,伦敦经济学院十一位诺贝尔经济奖得主的母校

sentences.en: Training ground for great economic thinkers like George Soros, and Friedrich Hayek, and Mick Jagger.
sentences.zh: 训练伟大经济学家的地方有乔治索罗斯、弗里德里希•哈耶克和滚石乐团的米克•贾格尔（笑声）

sentences.en: (Laughter) Last month, just last month, economists at LSE looked at 51 studies of pay-for-performance plans, inside of companies.
sentences.zh: 上个月，才刚过去的那个月政经学院的经济学家汇整了51个关于企业内部绩效薪酬的研究

sentences.en: Here's what they said: "We find that financial incentives can result in a negative impact on overall performance."
sentences.zh: 这些经济学家说，“我们发现金钱的诱因能对整体绩效带来负面效果。”

sentences.en: There is a mismatch between what science knows and what business does.
sentences.zh: 科学知识和商业行为之间有条鸿沟

sentences.en: And what worries me, as we stand here in the rubble of the economic collapse, is that too many organizations are making their decisions, their policies about talent and people, based on assumptions that are outdated,
sentences.zh: 我所忧心的是，在我们站在金融风暴废墟之间的此刻仍然有太多团体仍然以一些过时的、未经验证的、非科学的几乎是来自天方夜谭的假设

sentences.en: unexamined, and rooted more in folklore than in science.
sentences.zh: 来制定规则和管理人事

sentences.en: And if we really want to get out of this economic mess, if we really want high performance on those definitional tasks of the 21st century, the solution is not to do more of the wrong things,
sentences.zh: 如果我们真的想要摆脱这个经济危机如果我们真的想要在这些属于21世纪的核心工作中获取绩效的话这解答无异是错上加错：

sentences.en: to entice people with a sweeter carrot, or threaten them with a sharper stick.
sentences.zh: 用红萝卜来吸引人或是用棍子来威胁人

sentences.en: We need a whole new approach. The good news is that the scientists who've been studying motivation have given us this new approach.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一种新做法好消息是这些研究人类动机的科学家已经给了我们一个新方向

sentences.en: It's built much more around intrinsic motivation.
sentences.zh: 这个新方向讲求内在的诱因

sentences.en: Around the desire to do things because they matter, because we like it, they're interesting, or part of something important.
sentences.zh: 我们想做是因为它能改变世界因为我们喜欢，因为它很有趣因为它能影响的范围很广

sentences.en: And to my mind, that new operating system for our businesses revolves around three elements: autonomy, mastery and purpose.
sentences.zh: 在我心里，这种新的商业机制围绕在三个基础上自主性、掌握力和使命感

sentences.en: Autonomy: the urge to direct our own lives.
sentences.zh: 自主性，想要主掌自己人生的需求

sentences.en: Mastery: the desire to get better and better at something that matters.
sentences.zh: 掌握力，想要在举足轻重的事情上做得更好的欲望

sentences.en: Purpose: the yearning to do what we do in the service of something larger than ourselves.
sentences.zh: 使命感，希望我们所做的事情是为了更高远的理想的渴望

sentences.en: These are the building blocks of an entirely new operating system for our businesses.
sentences.zh: 这些便是建立新商业机制的基石

sentences.en: I want to talk today only about autonomy.
sentences.zh: 今天我只想提到自主性

sentences.en: In the 20th century, we came up with this idea of management.
sentences.zh: 20世纪产生了管理学的想法

sentences.en: Management did not emanate from nature. Management is not a tree, it's a television set.
sentences.zh: 管理学不是自然发生的管理学像是 － 它不是一棵树而是个电视机

sentences.en: Somebody invented it. It doesn't mean it's going to work forever.
sentences.zh: 对吗？有人发明它不代表它永远都好用

sentences.en: Management is great. Traditional notions of management are great if you want compliance.
sentences.zh: 管理学很好传统的管理学的概念是好的如果你需要的是服从

sentences.en: But if you want engagement, self-direction works better.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想要员工全心投入，自动自发更好有关自动自发，让我给你一些

sentences.en: Some examples of some kind of radical notions of self-direction.
sentences.zh: 革命性的例子代表着 --这样的例子不多

sentences.en: You don't see a lot of it, but you see the first stirrings of something really interesting going on, what it means is paying people adequately and fairly, absolutely -- getting the issue of money off the table,
sentences.zh: 但是你可以发现一些有趣的事情正开始发生它代表着付给人们合理与足够的工资让钱不再是问题然后给人们很大的自治权

sentences.en: and then giving people lots of autonomy.
sentences.zh: 让我举一些例子

sentences.en: Some examples. How many of you have heard of the company Atlassian?
sentences.zh: 在座谁听过一家叫 Atlassian 的公司？

sentences.en: It looks like less than half. (Laughter) Atlassian is an Australian software company.
sentences.zh: 看起来一半都不到（笑声）Atlassian 是一个澳大利亚的软件公司

sentences.en: And they do something incredibly cool. A few times a year they tell their engineers, "Go for the next 24 hours and work on anything you want, as long as it's not part of your regular job.
sentences.zh: 他们做了一件很酷的事一年有几次，他们跟公司里的软件工程师说“接下来的24个小时，去做你自己想做的事，只要它和你每天的工作无关

sentences.en: Work on anything you want." Engineers use this time to come up with a cool patch for code, come up with an elegant hack.
sentences.zh: 随便你要做什么都行。”这些工程师便利用这些时间写出一套有趣的编程，优雅地包装这些想法

sentences.en: Then they present all of the stuff that they've developed to their teammates, to the rest of the company, in this wild and woolly all-hands meeting at the end of the day.
sentences.zh: 在那天的最后在这个全员到齐，万众一心的会议中对他们的组员和整个公司介绍他的发明

sentences.en: Being Australians, everybody has a beer.
sentences.zh: 当然，身为澳大利亚人，大家都得来罐啤酒

sentences.en: They call them FedEx Days. Why? Because you have to deliver something overnight.
sentences.zh: 他们叫这是 FedEx 联邦快递日因为你必须在隔夜交出你的作品

sentences.en: It's pretty; not bad. It's a huge trademark violation, but it's pretty clever.
sentences.zh: 很不赖的想法。虽然违反商标法但这个想法很聪明。（笑声）

sentences.en: (Laughter) That one day of intense autonomy has produced a whole array of software fixes that might never have existed.
sentences.zh: 在高度自主的一日中他们做出了许多软件编程的革新之前根本没人想到的

sentences.en: It's worked so well that Atlassian has taken it to the next level with 20% time -- done, famously, at Google -- where engineers can spend 20% of their time working on anything they want.
sentences.zh: 这个计划的成功，让 Altlassian 更进一步的发明了五分之一时间谷歌把这个想法发扬光大工程师可以用五分之一的时间做所有他们想做的事情

sentences.en: They have autonomy over their time, their task, their team, their technique.
sentences.zh: 他们可以自由的分配他们的时间工作，组员，和作法

sentences.en: Radical amounts of autonomy. And at Google, as many of you know, about half of the new products in a typical year are birthed during that 20% time: things like Gmail, Orkut, Google News.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。完全的自主权诚如大家所知，在谷歌一年中有一半的新商品都来自这五分之一时间像谷歌信箱、Orkut、谷歌新闻

sentences.en: Let me give you an even more radical example of it: something called the Results Only Work Environment (the ROWE), created by two American consultants, in place at a dozen companies around North America.
sentences.zh: 让我给你一个更具革命性的例子一个叫做“只论结果的工作环境”简写是ROWE由两个美国分析师所创造用在十多家北美公司上

sentences.en: In a ROWE people don't have schedules. They show up when they want.
sentences.zh: 在 ROWE 之中，人们没有日程表他们想来就来

sentences.en: They don't have to be in the office at a certain time, or any time.
sentences.zh: 他们不需要在特定时间到公司任何时间

sentences.en: They just have to get their work done. How they do it, when they do it, where they do it, is totally up to them.
sentences.zh: 他们只需要把工作完成怎么做、何时做在哪里做、都取决于他们自己

sentences.en: Meetings in these kinds of environments are optional.
sentences.zh: 甚至连开会都是选择性的结果呢？

sentences.en: What happens? Almost across the board, productivity goes up, worker engagement goes up, worker satisfaction goes up, turnover goes down.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有公司的生产力都提升了工作投入度提升工作满意度提升，人力流失降低自主性、掌握力和使命感

sentences.en: Autonomy, mastery and purpose, the building blocks of a new way of doing things.
sentences.zh: 这便是新工作方式的新基础

sentences.en: Some of you might look at this and say, "Hmm, that sounds nice, but it's Utopian."
sentences.zh: 在座的某些人可能会看着然后说”嗯，听起来不错，就是太理想化了。“

sentences.en: And I say, "Nope. I have proof." The mid-1990s, Microsoft started an encyclopedia called Encarta.
sentences.zh: 我说”错了。我有证据。“在90年代中，微软开始了一个叫做 Encarta 的百科全书计划

sentences.en: They had deployed all the right incentives, They paid professionals to write and edit thousands of articles.
sentences.zh: 他们使用了所有正确的诱因所有的诱因。他们付钱给专业人士让他们写和编辑这些文章

sentences.en: Well-compensated managers oversaw the whole thing to make sure it came in on budget and on time.
sentences.zh: 收入颇丰的主管们监督着整个计划确定它不会超过预算和时间

sentences.en: A few years later, another encyclopedia got started.
sentences.zh: 几年后另一个百科全书计划开始了

sentences.en: Different model, right? Do it for fun. No one gets paid a cent, or a euro or a yen.
sentences.zh: 完全不同的模式为了兴趣而作。没有人能拿到任何一毛钱因为自己喜欢做而做

sentences.en: Do it because you like to do it. Just 10 years ago, if you had gone to an economist, anywhere, "Hey, I've got these two different models for creating an encyclopedia.
sentences.zh: 如果你在十年前到一个经济学家那里去对他说”我有两种撰写百科全书的模式

sentences.en: If they went head to head, who would win?"
sentences.zh: 拿来相比，谁会赢？“

sentences.en: 10 years ago you could not have found a single sober economist anywhere on planet Earth who would have predicted the Wikipedia model.
sentences.zh: 十年前你绝对不会找到任何一个清醒的经济学家在这个地球的任何角落能够预知维基百科的模式

sentences.en: This is the titanic battle between these two approaches.
sentences.zh: 这是一个两种模式之间的世纪战役

sentences.en: This is the Ali-Frazier of motivation, right?
sentences.zh: 动机的阿里与弗雷泽之战

sentences.en: This is the Thrilla in Manila. Intrinsic motivators versus extrinsic motivators.
sentences.zh: 就像那场在马尼拉的拳王之战是吗？内在动机和外在动机

sentences.en: Autonomy, mastery and purpose, versus carrot and sticks, and who wins?
sentences.zh: 自主性、掌握力和使命感和胡萝卜和棍子。谁赢了？

sentences.en: Intrinsic motivation, autonomy, mastery and purpose, in a knockout.
sentences.zh: 内在动机、自主性、掌握力和使命感

sentences.en: Let me wrap up. There is a mismatch between what science knows and what business does.
sentences.zh: 获得压倒性胜利。结论是科学知识和商业行为之间

sentences.en: Here is what science knows. One: Those 20th century rewards, those motivators we think are a natural part of business, do work, but only in a surprisingly narrow band of circumstances.
sentences.zh: 有条鸿沟一：这些20世纪的奖励这些我们当作商业中自然一部分的诱因是有用的。但意外地只在一个非常狭窄的情况下

sentences.en: Two: Those if-then rewards often destroy creativity.
sentences.zh: 二：这些奖励往往会破坏创造力

sentences.en: Three: The secret to high performance isn't rewards and punishments, but that unseen intrinsic drive-- the drive to do things for their own sake.
sentences.zh: 三：高绩效的秘密不是奖励和惩罚而是看不见的内在动力让人为了自己而做的动力

sentences.en: The drive to do things cause they matter.
sentences.zh: 让人有使命感的动力

sentences.en: And here's the best part. We already know this.
sentences.zh: 最好的是

sentences.en: The science confirms what we know in our hearts.
sentences.zh: 我们了然于心。科学不过确认了我们心里的声音

sentences.en: So, if we repair this mismatch between science and business, if we bring our motivation, notions of motivation into the 21st century, if we get past this lazy, dangerous, ideology
sentences.zh: 如果我们改变科学知识和商业行为之间有的那条鸿沟如果我们把我们的动机，对诱因的想法带进21世纪如果我们越过懒惰的、危险的、理想化的

sentences.en: of carrots and sticks, we can strengthen our businesses, we can solve a lot of those candle problems, and maybe, maybe -- we can change the world.
sentences.zh: 胡萝卜和棍子的想法我们可以强化我们的公司解决许多的“蜡烛问题”那么或许，或许，或许我们便能改变世界。

sentences.en: I rest my case. (Applause)
sentences.zh: 陈述完毕。（掌声）
